tagline: Down the old Robber's Pass to a reservoir of pumped water.
intro: Over Pacheco Pass, a low gap at 1,368 feet, Highway 152 crosses into Merced County and comes down the east side of the Diablo Range as a four-lane expressway. It runs along the north and east shore of San Luis Reservoir, passes between San Luis Dam and the O'Neill Forebay, and goes on to meet Interstate 5.
The road is older than it looks. Butterfield Overland Mail coaches came through from 1858 to 1861, and in the 1850s travelers knew the place as Robber's Pass, after the hold-ups.

moments.title: Pacheco State Park
moments.text: The last piece of a rancho the Pacheco family held from 1843, left to the state by a descendant. Its trails look out over both valleys, with wildflowers in spring.

moments.title: San Luis Reservoir
moments.text: The Romero Overlook visitor center looks over the largest off-stream reservoir in the country, filled with Delta water pumped uphill from the forebay below.

moments.title: O'Neill Forebay
moments.text: The water pumped up into the big reservoir comes back down here through a power plant, and the high-voltage lines cross the forebay on man-made islands.
